text:
Alex M.: Heads-up — I'm leaving Redwood at the end of next month. Need advice: considering a 401(k) withdrawal for a house down payment vs rolling to an IRA. What happens tax/penalty-wise on separation? Any deadline/lock periods I should know about? @people-ops
Sara (People Ops): Congrats on the next step, Alex! :tada: Quick summary: you can take a distribution after separation or roll the balance to an IRA/401k at the new employer. Rollovers avoid immediate taxes/penalties. Withdrawals may be taxable and could incur a 10% early-withdrawal penalty if you're under 59½ (with some exceptions).
Alex M.: Thanks. Is there any company window where the 401k administrator holds funds or delays processing after termination? Trying to coordinate timing with an offer expiration for the house.
Ben - Payroll: Not usually — once HR sends termination + final comp, the plan admin (Vanguard/Better?) processes distribution/rollover requests. Typical timeline: admin acknowledgement within 5 business days, distribution/rollover completed ~7–14 business days after request, sometimes longer if forms are mailed.
Linda (Finance): Also FYI — if you request a direct rollover to an IRA, funds go straight from the plan to the IRA (no tax withheld). If you take a check payable to you, the plan will withhold mandatory 20% federal tax for a taxable distribution. You'd have to make up that 20% when rolling to avoid taxes.
Alex M.: Good to know. Any option to do a partial rollover so I can take only what I need? I want to preserve most funds for retirement.
Sara (People Ops): Most plans allow partial distributions. We can give you the distribution form and the admin's checklist. If you do partial cash-out, confirm with the plan admin whether they require a minimum leftover balance.
TaxBot: Quick note from IRS rules: if you separate in the year you turn 55 or older and the distribution is from the employer plan, the 10% early-distribution penalty may not apply (the "separation from service" rule). Check your birth year vs separation date.
Alex M.: I'm 33 so that exception won't apply. If I do a rollover to an IRA and then withdraw from the IRA for the down payment, are there penalties?
Linda (Finance): IRAs have different rules. Traditional IRA withdrawals before 59½ generally incur taxes + 10% penalty. Roth conversions and qualified first-time homebuyer exceptions exist but are limited (Roth contributions vs conversions timing matters). Recommend talking to a tax advisor for your scenario.
Ben - Payroll: One more operational note: if you want a direct rollover, include the receiving account details (IRA custodian name, account number, EIN). If you want a trustee-to-trustee transfer we can coordinate with the plan admin.
Sara (People Ops): Action items: Alex — DM me your desired outcome (rollover vs partial cash-out) and I'll pull the distribution paperwork and estimated timeline from the plan admin. If you want, I can also queue a consult with our benefits vendor rep this week.
Alex M.: Please queue the paperwork and vendor consult. I'd like a partial rollover + small withdrawal. Also please confirm if there are any blackout/maintenance windows coming up this quarter that might delay processing.
Ben - Payroll: Will check plan admin maintenance schedule and flag any known blackouts. If we see anything, we'll expedite before your termination date.
Sara (People Ops): Got it. I'll DM you the forms and loop in Ben and Linda if we need approvals. Expect vendor availability times in the doc. :email:
